coverage.independent_answers: Elementary order laws, explicit root/child finite-tree countermodels, and regular zeroSpine witness; no second Boolean implementation.
coverage.path_boundary: Entry points are observed; successful guarded calls do not certify raw branch execution. Only kind=raw directly invokes the two-branch backend. Tags identify fixture groups, not a runtime trace.

limits.compile_error_boundary: NOT RUN and nonzero checker exit; overall NOT RUN unless a mismatch is observed
limits.execution: one fresh Lean process group per fixture, sequentially; entire group killed and reaped on timeout

rows.justification: Every tree is below itself; no premise is needed.
rows.name: empty-reflexive

rows.justification: Set v0 to the root-only tree product(bottom,bottom), v1 to bottom, and use the empty address.
rows.name: empty-variable-cross

rows.justification: Bottom has no product nodes, so bottom is below every tree.
rows.name: empty-bottom-left

rows.justification: Set v0 to the root-only tree product(bottom,bottom); it has the empty node and bottom does not.
rows.name: empty-variable-bottom

rows.justification: Set v0 to the root-only tree. product(v0,bottom) has the false-left child while v0 does not.
rows.name: empty-product-left

rows.justification: The queried inequality is exactly the listed premise.
rows.name: premise-forward

rows.justification: Set v0 to bottom and v1 to the root-only tree. The premise holds, but v1 is not below v0 at the empty address.
rows.name: premise-reverse

rows.justification: Both listed premises compose by transitivity; the queried pair is not itself a premise.
rows.name: transitive-query-not-premise

rows.justification: Product is covariant in both arguments, and bottom is below itself; apply product_mono to the premise.
rows.name: product-monotone

rows.justification: Set v0 to bottom and v1 to the root-only tree. The premise holds, while the queried products differ at the left child.
rows.name: product-monotone-reverse

rows.justification: The query-only v2 is root-only, v0 is bottom, and v1 is root-only; the premise holds but the query fails at the empty address.
rows.name: query-only-source

rows.justification: Set v0 and v1 to the root-only tree and query-only v2 to bottom; the premise holds but the query fails at the empty address.
rows.name: query-only-target

rows.justification: With zero original variables, bottom is still below itself.
rows.name: zero-vars-empty-reflexive

rows.justification: The product has its root node by definition while bottom has no nodes; there are no valuations to restrict this result.
rows.name: zero-vars-product-bottom

rows.justification: The only premise is impossible because product(bottom,bottom) contains its root and bottom does not; entailment is vacuous.
rows.name: unsat-zero-variable-query

rows.justification: The same variable-free impossible premise has no model, so the unrelated query v0 <= bottom is vacuously entailed.
rows.name: unsat-query-variable

rows.justification: Set v0 to the root-only tree. bottom <= v0 holds, but v0 <= bottom fails at the empty address.
rows.name: bottom-premise-reverse

rows.justification: Bottom is below every product tree, independently of v0.
rows.name: bottom-to-product

rows.justification: The same product occurs on both sides of a premise and in the query; reflexivity is independent of slot allocation.
rows.name: duplicate-product-reflexive

rows.justification: Set v0=bottom, v1=bottom, and v2 to product(root-only,bottom). The premise holds at every address, but v2 has a false-left child absent from product(v0,v1).
rows.name: duplicate-product-reverse

rows.justification: A nested product expression is repeated exactly; reflexivity remains valid with duplicate product occurrences.
rows.name: nested-duplicate-reflexive

rows.justification: Apply the premise twice and product covariance; the duplicated variable children are intentional.
rows.name: duplicate-product-derived

rows.justification: The regular zeroSpine tree satisfies product(zeroSpine,bottom) <= zeroSpine and has the empty node, so it refutes zeroSpine <= bottom. The premise also forces arbitrarily long false spines in every model.
rows.name: necessarily-infinite-zero-spine

rows.justification: The queried inequality is the premise, even though its models include the regular infinite zeroSpine model.
rows.name: necessarily-infinite-premise

rows.justification: This repeats the product from the premise in the reversed query; the explicit root-plus-left-child v2 countermodel separates the directions.
rows.name: query-not-premise-reverse-product

rows.justification: Set v0 to root-only and v1 to bottom. The two products disagree at the first child address.
rows.name: empty-product-swap

rows.justification: The normalized variable instance has the root-only/bottom countermodel at the empty address.
rows.name: raw-empty-cross

rows.justification: The variable inequality is explicitly present in the normalized premise list.
rows.name: raw-premise-forward

rows.justification: The root-only/bottom valuation satisfies 0 <= 1 but refutes 1 <= 0 at the empty address.
rows.name: raw-premise-reverse

rows.justification: The raw two-branch backend must preserve reflexivity without a frontend guard.
rows.name: raw-reflexive

rows.justification: Denial forces v0 below bottom, while lower requires product(v0,v0) below v0; these conflict at the product root, but reflexivity remains true.
rows.name: raw-unsat-denial-lower

rows.justification: The two listed inequalities establish both directions; query the reverse one without a frontend guard.
rows.name: raw-equality-both-directions

rows.justification: Take v1=root-only and v0=product(v1,v1). The upper premise holds by equality, but v0 has a child absent from v1.
rows.name: raw-upper-only

rows.justification: The normalized fast path sees a root-only/bottom countermodel at the empty address.
rows.name: normalized-empty-cross

rows.justification: The queried normalized leq clause is explicitly present.
rows.name: normalized-premise-forward

rows.justification: A root-only/bottom valuation satisfies the premise and refutes the reversed query.
rows.name: normalized-premise-reverse

rows.justification: This calls the guarded normalized entry point directly, so its reflexivity guard returns true.
rows.name: normalized-reflexive

rows.justification: The normalized constraints are contradictory at the product root; reflexivity remains valid.
rows.name: normalized-unsat-denial-lower
